title: BotPsy: On-Device Personal Assistant with a Sub-Billion-Parameter Agentic Language Model
Delaying Internal Deployments Until After X Days of Safety Testing
summary: This post reflects my own takes, and not that of my employer's. This is a simple idea: before a new model can be deployed internally, you must first test it for a minimum, fixed period. You can adjust various axes of this proposal: Duration of the wait: in calendar time, or until you fulfill some condition. What it blocks: external deployment, internal deployment, or the training of future checkpoints. When the fixed period starts: from the first checkpoint, the final checkpoint, or any checkpoint that is “sufficiently similar / representative” to the one that is ultimately deployed. One concrete target that I like is: “No checkpoint may be used internally for purposes beyond safety testing, until at least X calendar days after its hash is filed with an auditor.” This is one specific implementation of internal deployment lags, an idea that the AI Futures Project (AIFP) briefly discusses in How to pace the US frontier as “AI R&D can only be conducted or assisted by AIs that were trained at least 9 months ago”. What does this look like when implemented? Let’s run through a scenario to pin down the details of this proposal. The places where it could go wrong are in the open questions at the end. A legislative body sets a minimum waiting period of X calendar days (starting at 10 and possibly ratcheting up to 90). title: How I'm thinking about different types of automated alignment
summary: I used to think of "automating alignment" as a natural category. But when I tried to think through the strategic implications, I realised that it depends a lot on the type of work. I'm now thinking of it in three buckets: Empirical alignment research : design and execution of alignment-relevant experiments (for a given notion of what we’re aiming for) Conceptual alignment research: theoretical or judgement-driven work to improve our understanding of what we’re aiming for and how to achieve it (including how to measure it) Direct alignment work : making particular AI systems more aligned (including via inputs such as training data) In the rest of this post I'll walk through my current takes on these in terms what’s needed for automation, how good or bad they look, what our priorities might be (to the extent we're interested in automating alignment [1] ), etc. Automating empirical alignment research This is the most obvious fit for the AI capabilities we’re getting at the moment. You want to know more about the relationship between some alignment-relevant variables? Great, an AI agent can design and run that experiment for you. You want to know what training methods help your alignment benchmark go up? In the not-too-distant future, AI agents will probably be able to do this too. When we have the automated capabilities researchers we seem on track for, this is exactly the kind of thing they’ll likely be able to do a lot of. Note that I’m not counting the design of benchmarks/me
